<reason>Both sides were well-grounded (A's Chicago heat-wave use tracks real scholarship; B avoided fake precision) and both formatted Q/A rounds correctly. A built a real case: infrastructure is the substrate every app success routes into, stacked multi-use returns (never answered), app churn, and late hours directly serving mobile lonely people. But B controlled the back half. B's pressure questions forced A to concede that extended hours "don't teleport the never-visitor" and that the finding work runs through referrals and outreach — concessions B converted into "sensors only sense members" and "that is an outreach list. Fund the list." B also answered A's best pressure directly (the registry is referral-fed and volunteer-side, not opt-in) and reframed the motion as a marginal-dollar choice between an eleventh hour of lighting and a first phone call. A's closing line "the doorbell takes care of itself" was hung on the Chicago anecdote in B's closer — the debate's most decisive moment. A kept live routes (destination logic, churn, teens/night-shift workers, where B's "they have phones" reply was thin), and B's clipped Rebuttal 1 is a small execution cost, so the win is clear but competitive rather than dominant.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's Turn 6 pressure questions → A's Turn 7 concessions → B's Turn 8 weaponization: extracting "hours don't teleport the never-visitor," compressing it into "sensors only sense members," and flipping A's library-outreach answer into "that is an outreach list. Fund the list," while directly answering A's opt-in objection with the referral-fed, volunteer-side registry.</best_rebuttal>
